en: Most shops around here open early
in the morning and close by evening.
My own hat shop is no exception.
I hope to see you tomorrow morning.
, sir...
Er, the hat you bought from me suits you
very well indeed.
I've worn this hat for many years.
O-oh, is that so? Well, they're so alike
that I couldn't tell them apart...
Next time, do wear the hat you bought
from my shop as well, sir.
And you, sir, look to me to be old enough
to be called a true gentleman.
In this country, a hat marks a gentleman.
By all means, do buy one before you go.
Hmm, I wonder if a hat would even suit me.
Any hat at all would suit you, sir.
I guarantee it.
You have such striking good looks.
I look forward to your next visit.
No, I'm afraid a mere youngster like me
isn't ready for a silk hat yet...
I see... What a pity.
When you enter society, sir, I do hope
you'll place your order with me...
It's all high-class shops.
note: Follows #2630 'This district caters to gentlemen of rank.'

en: In a few years, when you need a hat,
Please come again.
note: Variant lowercase for Clement msg 91471 after #2668.

en: You're welcome at my shop any time.
Is someone there?
Sorry to startle you.
I suddenly need a hat, so I came to place
an order.
I see. My, you gave me quite a fright.
It's the middle of the night, after all.
Your business must be very urgent indeed.
Sorry to rush you, but please show me
a few of your hat designs.
Certainly.
I'll bring them out right away.
I'm sorry...
Wah, wh-, wh-wh-wh-wh...
Whaaaaaat?!
Sorry it wasn't a hat I came to order.
, my master. Welcome.
note: After the name (servant mode, as #0/#854); #855 starts a new line.

en: Oh dear, I've cut my finger
And I take such good care of my fingertips.
I have been awaiting you.
I am ready to receive your orders.
Hmm, I'm short on sleep, somehow.
I suppose I'm not young anymore.
Good day, and welcome.
Something tailored? What would you like?
Is this a tailor's?
That's right. I'm the proprietor, Percy.
30 years in the trade. Pleased to meet you.
Dinner jackets, silk shirts, you name it.
I see.
note: Player; shared with Justin 160815 and Abraham 168635.

en: Then perhaps I'll have a shirt made.
Why, thank you very much.
Then let me take your measurements.
And may I have your name, sir?
I leave it in your hands, then.
We meet again. Here for some tailoring?
You look well.
So you're a tailor.
Yes, indeed. I'm Percy, the owner.
And may I have your name once more, sir?
I'm always at your service for tailoring.
Ah,
note: Before the name; #2545 ', sir.' follows: 'Ah, {NAME}, sir.'

en: Your order isn't ready yet, I'm afraid.
Please wait just a little longer.
Some dreadful things have been happening
note: #152 '...' comes before on the same line.

en: in this city lately, it seems.
The folk in the poor quarters are terrified.
The upper classes seem quite unconcerned.
Why the difference, I wonder?
Oh, I've said too much. Forgive me.
